title: LinkedIn profile checklist
intro: 12 checks. Fix photo, name and headline first: they are all a partner sees before opening your profile. I’d do all 12 in one sitting, laptop open, before you send a single request.
intro_phone: 12 checks. Fix photo, name and headline first: open your profile, fix one check, come back and tick it. I’d do all 12 in one sitting, before you send a single request.

open.label: Open my profile
open.hint:
Keep it beside this page and tick each check as you fix it.
Before your first edit: Settings & Privacy › Visibility › Visibility of your LinkedIn activity › Share profile updates off, so your network isn’t told about each change; on again when you’re done.
Link opens the browser? In the LinkedIn app, tap your photo › View profile.

items.check: A clear head-and-shoulders photo of you
items.how: Your profile › your photo › upload the new one › Save photo.
example: ✅ Face a window, plain light wall behind you, phone at eye level. Your face fills most of the square. Natural smile, eyes to the camera.
✅ A formal shirt, kurta or top. You don’t need a blazer.
❌ Arm’s-length selfie, a function photo, a crop from a group picture, sunglasses, filters.
Background cleaned up with an app? Fine. A changed face is not: it must look like you on interview day. Test: at fingernail size, as it shows next to your request, is it still clearly you?

Visibility (on a laptop): your photo › Visibility › All LinkedIn members or Public, and Public profile & URL › Your profile’s public visibility On. Set to connections only, a partner who isn’t connected yet can’t see your photo.
Use the same photo on Gmail and WhatsApp, so HR knows the mail and the call are the same person.

items.check: Your name exactly as on your CV, with nothing before it
items.how: Your profile › the pencil in your intro › First name, Last name.
example: ✅ Ishita Sharma: the same spelling as your CV, ICAI’s SSP portal and Gmail.
❌ CA Ishita Sharma · Semi CA Ishita · Ishita Sharma (CA Finalist) · Aspiring CA
“CA Finalist” is a word you search with (LinkedIn search links), not one you write about yourself.
Only ICAI members may put “CA” before their name; a partner who sees it on a CA Inter profile stops reading. Your stage goes in the headline.

items.check: Headline: your stage, target, city and one proof
items.how: Your profile › the pencil in your intro › Headline.
example: It shows under your name in every search and invitation.
Location (same screen): the city you want articleship in. A search filtered to Pune finds only profiles that say Pune.
Open to two cities? Location is the one you’d pick first; put both at the end of your headline: … | Pune or Mumbai.
✅ **My pick, if you cleared in one go:** CA Inter cleared ([Month Year]) | First attempt | Seeking articleship in {domain|statutory audit} | Pune
✅ CA Inter cleared (Group I [Month Year], Group II [Month Year]) | Seeking articleship in {domain|audit} | Delhi NCR
✅ CA Inter result awaited ([Month Year]) | ICITSS done | Seeking articleship in {domain|audit} | Kolkata
❌ Aspiring CA | Finance enthusiast | Learner: nothing anyone searches for.
❌ CA Finalist || Hardworking || Dedicated: a title you don’t hold yet, and words nobody types.

One proof, right after your stage: something a partner can check. A job simulation you finished, “ICITSS done, can join from [Month]”, a first attempt, your college. A rank (AIR) only with your rank letter. Nothing yet? Leave it out.

Keep “CA Inter” and the exam month in: they are the words people search for. Test it: search “articleship {domain|statutory audit} Pune” › People. Are you there? Read the top five results: yours should be the clearest of them.
Change it the day your status changes: result, ICITSS, selection.
items.copy: CA Inter cleared ([Month Year]) | [proof] | Seeking articleship in [domain] | [City]

items.check: Your profile address is just your name
items.how: Your profile › Public profile & URL › Edit your custom URL › Save.
example: ✅ linkedin.com/in/ishita-sharma
Taken? Add an initial or your city: ishita-k-sharma, ishita-sharma-pune.
❌ The default with random characters (ishita-sharma-4b7a91203), a nickname, your birth year.
Put it on your CV and Gmail signature, as in the CV checklist, and tap it once in your CV PDF on your phone.

items.check: About: the opening lines say who you are, what you’ve done and what you want
items.how: Your profile › Add profile section › Core › About.
example: Only the first few lines show before “…see more”. Many readers stop there.
> I cleared CA Intermediate in May. I’m looking for articleship in {domain|statutory audit} in Pune.
> {proof}
> I want to learn audit working papers where seniors review my work. Write to me at ishita.sharma@email.com.
Helped a CA office or a family business? Put that in place of the [One thing…] line, with a number, only if you really did it.
Result awaited? Line 1: “My CA Intermediate result ([Month Year]) is awaited; I’ve finished ICITSS and I’m looking for articleship in …”

Below them, if you like: how you used your exam break, one college role, a line of search words (Statutory audit · Vouching · Excel · Tally Prime), and once your joining date is fixed, “I can join from [Month Year].”
❌ “Passionate, hardworking, dedicated professional”, copied hobbies, one long paragraph, “he” or “she”.
Write in “I”, one line for each part, and only lines you can talk about for two minutes in an interview. Read it on your phone before saving.
items.copy:
I cleared CA Intermediate in [Month Year]. I’m looking for articleship in [domain] in [City].
[One thing you have actually done, in your CV’s words; a number if it has one.]
I want to learn [what you want to learn]. Write to me at [email].

items.check: ICAI and your college in Education, picked from the list so their logos show; ranks in Honors
items.how: Add profile section › Core › Education › type “The Institute of Chartered Accountants of India” and pick it from the list.
example: Why: people who search by school (ICAI, your college) find you.
Two entries come up? Pick the one with ICAI’s logo: on your profile it should then open ICAI’s own school page.

Degree: CA Intermediate. Description: “Both groups cleared ([Month Year]) · ICITSS completed”, or one line per group with its month and year. Paper exemptions only if you got them, worded as on your CV.
Add your college the same way: B.Com, years, “pursuing” if you haven’t finished. CA Foundation as a second ICAI entry if you like.
Marks: the same figures as your CV, never rounded up, or leave them out.
❌ ICAI under Experience. Studying at ICAI is not a job at ICAI.
Honors & awards: ranks, a prize, in the same wording as your CV (Add profile section › Additional).

items.check: Courses and simulations in Licenses & certifications; Experience only for real work
items.how: Add profile section › Recommended › Licenses & certifications. Pick the issuer from the list so its logo shows.
example: ✅ PwC US Audit Job Simulation · issuer Forage
✅ PwC US Tax Job Simulation · issuer Forage
✅ Goldman Sachs Excel Skills for Business Job Simulation · issuer Forage
✅ SEBI Investor Awareness Test (Level 1) · issuer National Institute of Securities Markets (NISM)
Issue date: the month you finished. Expiry: only if your certificate shows one. Credential ID and URL if it has them (on Forage, the code and link at the certificate’s foot), and the PDF as media.

Only what you’ve finished: a course goes on in the month you complete it. Same names and months as your CV: an Excel certificate dated before your exams, beside a CV that says you learnt Excel after them, becomes an interview question.
The MSC Articleship Program line goes on your CV, not here.
❌ Under Experience or Internship. A simulation is not a job.

Experience: only real work; none yet, leave it empty. Helped in a CA office or a family business? Say what you did and how much: “Matched 120 purchase invoices with GSTR-2B for six clients; flagged 9 mismatches.”

items.check: One piece of your own work pinned in Featured
items.how: Add profile section › Recommended › Add featured › + › a document or a link.
example: Best: an Excel reconciliation you built, or a short post explaining one idea in your own words. **My pick:** the reconciliation, as a one-page PDF.
No certificate for it? Add it under Projects too (Add profile section › Recommended › Projects), with the same PDF.
Before you upload, delete your phone number, address and any real person’s or client’s name. One strong item beats five weak ones. Not your CV: it carries your phone number.
Nothing to show yet? Publish your result post, pin it, and swap it for a work sample later.
items.copy:
Cleared CA Intermediate ([Month Year]).
What worked: [one study habit] and [one revision habit].
Thank you, [teacher’s name], for [one specific thing].
Next: articleship in [domain] in [City].

items.check: Three skills you can prove, each linked to where you used it
items.how: Add profile section › Core › Skills, then tick the boxes for the entries where you used each one.
example: Open one real articleship opening in your domain and note the skills it asks for. Pick three you can show, e.g. Vouching · Microsoft Excel · GST returns.
Use the opening’s own words in your headline and About too: for an audit team, “statutory audit”, not just “finance”.
❌ Teamwork, Communication, Leadership as the skills you lead with. Everyone has them; nobody searches for them.

items.check: Open to Work: articleship, your cities, start date, all members
items.how: Your profile › Open to › Finding a new job.
example: Job titles: Article Assistant, and Articled Assistant if the list offers it. Locations: only cities you can reach for an interview.
Employment types: Full-time, plus Internship if the list offers it. Location types: On-site.
Start date: the option closest to when you can really join (Notice period too, if your form shows it).
Who can see it: All LinkedIn members. “Recruiters only” hides you from partners who post openings themselves. The #OpenToWork frame is fine.

While you’re there: Jobs › Preferences › Resumes and application data › upload the CV PDF you mail firms, named as in the CV checklist. Don’t add your CV to your profile itself: anyone in your network can download it.

items.check: Email in Contact info, a plain banner, your phone number nowhere public
items.how: Your profile › Contact info › the pencil.
example: Contact info: your name-based email, e.g. ishita.sharma@email.com. Only connections see it; a partner who hasn’t accepted yet finds it in your About and on your CV. Phone field: empty.
Banner: a plain colour, one simple line such as “Statutory audit · Excel · Pune”, or a real photo of you presenting. Keep the left third empty: your photo sits on it.
❌ Your phone number on the banner or in About: anyone can see it, and scam calls follow. HR will take it from your CV.
❌ Quotes, city skylines, logos of firms you don’t work at.

items.check: One recommendation from someone who has seen your work
items.how: Connect first. Their profile › More › Request a recommendation › how you know them › Position at the time (no job? ICAI or college, if listed) › paste › Send.
example: Who: your ICITSS faculty member, a teacher, your project guide, the CA you helped; not a friend or relative. **My pick:** your ICITSS faculty member.
❌ “I’ll write one if you write one”, or writing it for them to paste. The request below gives them the facts and makes “no” easy.
For [what you did with them], e.g. “I presented in your ICITSS batch”. When it’s up: “Thank you, Sir. I’ve added it, and I’ll tell you where I join.” Ma’am for a woman, in both.
items.copy:
[Name] Sir,
I’m applying for articleship in [domain].
Would you write me a short LinkedIn recommendation?
In case it helps: in [Month Year] [what you did with them].
Two or three lines are plenty. If you’re busy, no problem at all.
Thank you, [Your name]

notes.title: Same story as your CV
notes.text: Your profile › More › Save to PDF (on a laptop). It’s the file HR forwards. Read it line by line next to your CV: result month and groups, marks, certificate months, projects, city. A date that doesn’t match becomes the first interview question.

done.title: All 12 ticked?
done.text: Next, today: run the Posts search for your city, apply to anything that fits the same day, and note the partner or HR person behind each opening.

proof_now: In the PwC US Audit Job Simulation (Forage) I walked through a client’s purchasing process and built a risk-control matrix.

work_simulation._what: Release 2 only (row 1.6). The tool's WORK_SIMULATION_LIVE flag (and build.py --ws-live) apply this: each swap puts its line in place of the release-1 line named in 'for'; copy is the Copy box text once a domain is set; also is a second link; proofs are the About line per domain. Release 1 reads none of it.

swap.for: One proof, right after your stage: something a partner can check. A job simulation you finished, “ICITSS done, can join from [Month]”, a first attempt, your college. A rank (AIR) only with your rank letter. Nothing yet? Leave it out.
swap.line: One proof, right after your stage: something a partner can check. A Work Simulation you finished, “ICITSS done, can join from [Month]”, a first attempt, your college. A rank (AIR) only with your rank letter. Nothing yet? Leave it out.

headline.copy: CA Inter cleared ([Month Year]) | {sim} Work Simulation | Seeking articleship in [domain] | [City]

about.copy:
I cleared CA Intermediate in [Month Year]. I’m looking for articleship in [domain] in [City].
In my {sim} Work Simulation I [one task you did, with a number].
I want to learn [what you want to learn]. Write to me at [your email].

swap.for: Best: an Excel reconciliation you built, or a short post explaining one idea in your own words. **My pick:** the reconciliation, as a one-page PDF.
swap.line: Best: your Work Simulation work sample (the vouching sheet with your findings), an Excel reconciliation you built, or a short post explaining one idea in your own words. **My pick:** the work sample, as a one-page PDF.

also.label: Work Simulation (pick a finished level › Print work sample)

proofs.statutory-audit: In my Statutory Audit Work Simulation I vouched 20 purchase bills against orders, receipt notes and ledgers and flagged 5 cut-off, approval and GST exceptions.
proofs.internal-audit: In my Internal Audit Work Simulation I walked one purchase end to end, tested approval and three-way-match controls on 15 purchases and wrote 2 observations.
proofs.direct-tax: In my Direct Tax Work Simulation I checked 8 tax-audit items (cash payments, TDS, late statutory dues, depreciation) against the books and drafted the notes.
proofs.gst: In my GST Work Simulation I prepared GSTR-1 and GSTR-3B workings for a month of 12 invoices and checked input tax credit against GSTR-2B.
proofs.bank-audit: In my Bank Audit Work Simulation I recomputed drawing power for 1 cash-credit account and classified 10 accounts by days overdue.
proofs.transfer-pricing: In my Transfer Pricing Work Simulation I screened 14 comparables, computed margins and the range, and tested the client's margin.
proofs.ma-tax: In my M&A Tax Work Simulation I compared dividend, buyback and capital reduction for a group company and wrote a one-page note on the tax angle of each.
proofs.valuation: In my Valuation Work Simulation I cleaned a 3-year P&L to EBITDA and built a DCF with three inputs and one sensitivity.
proofs.fdd: In my FDD Work Simulation I normalised EBITDA for 5 adjustments, trended working capital, listed net debt and three red flags.
proofs.forensic: In my Forensic Work Simulation I analysed a 500-row ledger and flagged duplicates, round sums, holiday entries and vendor–employee matches.
proofs.consulting: In my Consulting Work Simulation I broke a profit fall into price, volume and cost drivers and made one recommendation.
proofs.accounting: In my Accounting Work Simulation I closed a month's books from vouchers to a trial balance and Schedule III statements, with a bank reconciliation.
proofs.ib-er: In my IB & ER Work Simulation I wrote a one-page company profile and a target screen with a valuation summary.
